message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Release Packages

# CONPY-317: build the release artifacts here instead of by hand.
#
# 1.1 ships a single distribution, 'mariadb', and it is the C extension: the
# sdist and every binary wheel carry that same name. (2.0 splits the connector
# into mariadb / mariadb-c / mariadb-pool / mariadb-binary and its workflow has
# one build job per distribution; there is nothing to split here.)

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      connector_c_version:
        description: 'MariaDB Connector/C version to build against'
        required: false
        default: '3.4.11'
        type: string
      publish_to:
        description: 'Publish to'
        required: true
        default: 'testpypi'
        type: choice
        options:
          - testpypi
          - pypi
          - none

env:
  MARIADB_CONNECTOR_C_VERSION: ${{ github.event.inputs.connector_c_version || '3.4.11' }}
  MYSQL_TEST_HOST: mariadb.example.com
  MYSQL_TEST_PORT: 3306
  MYSQL_TEST_USER: root
  MYSQL_TEST_PASSWD: "heyPassw-!*20oRd"
  MYSQL_TEST_DB: testp

jobs:
  # Source distribution
  build-sdist:
    name: Build mariadb (sdist)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Cache pip dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pip-

      # setup.py reads the Connector/C configuration through mariadb_config at
      # import time, so the development files are needed even to pack an sdist.
      - name: Install MariaDB Connector/C development files
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libmariadb-dev

      - name: Install build dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install build setuptools wheel packaging

      - name: Build sdist
        run: |
          python -m build --sdist --outdir dist/

      - name: Upload artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: mariadb-sdist
          path: dist/

  # Binary wheels - Windows
  build-wheels-windows:
    name: Build mariadb wheel (Windows ${{ matrix.arch }} ${{ matrix.pyver }})
    runs-on: windows-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        arch: [win_amd64, win32]
        pyver: [cp311, cp312, cp313, cp314, cp315]
        # These entries only add keys to the combinations above: the
        # cibuildwheel architecture and the cmake generator platform.
        include:
          - arch: win_amd64
            cibw_arch: AMD64
            cmake_arch: x64
          - arch: win32
            cibw_arch: x86
            cmake_arch: Win32

    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      - name: Add hosts entry
        shell: bash
        run: echo "127.0.0.1 mariadb.example.com" >> /c/Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts

      - name: Setup MariaDB Server
        id: setup-mariadb-windows
        uses: rusher/action-setup-mariadb@master
        with:
          tag: '11.4'
          root-password: ${{ env.MYSQL_TEST_PASSWD }}
          user: ${{ env.MYSQL_TEST_USER }}
          password: ${{ env.MYSQL_TEST_PASSWD }}
          database: ${{ env.MYSQL_TEST_DB }}

      - name: Cache MariaDB Connector/C build
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: C:\mariadb-connector-c.build
          key: mariadb-connector-c-${{ env.MARIADB_CONNECTOR_C_VERSION }}-windows-${{ matrix.cmake_arch }}

      - name: Build wheels
        uses: pypa/cibuildwheel@v4.3.0
        env:
          TEST_DB_USER: 'root'
          TEST_DB_HOST: ${{ env.MYSQL_TEST_HOST }}
          TEST_DB_DATABASE: ${{ env.MYSQL_TEST_DB }}
          TEST_DB_PORT: ${{ env.MYSQL_TEST_PORT }}
          TEST_DB_PASSWORD: ${{ env.MYSQL_TEST_PASSWD }}
          CIBW_BUILD: ${{matrix.pyver}}-${{matrix.arch}}
          CIBW_ARCHS_WINDOWS: ${{ matrix.cibw_arch }}
          # Read by build_connector_c_windows.bat, which cibuildwheel runs
          # directly on the runner, so the job environment is visible to it.
          CMAKE_ARCH: ${{ matrix.cmake_arch }}
          CIBW_BEFORE_ALL_WINDOWS: >-
            cmd /c "{project}\tools\ci\build_connector_c_windows.bat"
          CIBW_REPAIR_WHEEL_COMMAND_WINDOWS: >-
            delvewheel repair -w {dest_dir} {wheel}
          CIBW_TEST_REQUIRES: pytest
          # -o addopts= : pyproject sets addopts "-ra -q --tb=short", whose -q
          # cancels the -v below, so a crash is reported as an anonymous dot.
          # -s : pytest captures stderr at the file-descriptor level, so an
          # abort's message would otherwise die in the capture buffer.
          CIBW_TEST_COMMAND: >-
            pytest {project}/testing/test/integration --color yes -v -s -o addopts=
          CIBW_ENVIRONMENT_PASS_WINDOWS: TEST_DB_USER TEST_DB_HOST TEST_DB_DATABASE TEST_DB_PORT TEST_DB_PASSWORD MARIADB_CC_INSTALL_DIR MARIADB_CONNECTOR_C_VERSION
          CIBW_ENVIRONMENT_WINDOWS: >-
            PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1
            LOCAL_DB=${{ steps.setup-mariadb-windows.outputs.database-type }}
            MARIADB_CC_INSTALL_DIR=C:\\mariadb-connector-c.build
            PATH="C:\\mariadb-connector-c.build\\bin;$PATH"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: windows-${{matrix.pyver}}-${{matrix.arch}}
          path: ./wheelhouse/*.whl

  # Merge every wheel into one artifact
  merge-wheels:
    name: Merge mariadb wheels
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-wheels-windows]

    steps:
      - name: Merge artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact/merge@v7
        with:
          name: mariadb-wheels
          pattern: "windows-*"
          delete-merged: true

  # Publish to TestPyPI (release candidate or manual trigger)
  publish-testpypi:
    name: Publish mariadb to TestPyPI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-sdist, merge-wheels]
    if: |
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.publish_to == 'testpypi') ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && contains(github.event.release.tag_name, 'rc'))
    environment: testpypi
    permissions:
      id-token: write

    steps:
      - name: Download artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: mariadb-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: dist/

      - name: Publish mariadb to TestPyPI
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
        with:
          repository-url: https://test.pypi.org/legacy/
          packages-dir: dist/
          skip-existing: true
          verbose: true

  # Publish to PyPI (release only or manual trigger)
  publish-pypi:
    name: Publish mariadb to PyPI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-sdist, merge-wheels]
    if: |
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.publish_to == 'pypi') ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && !contains(github.event.release.tag_name, 'rc'))
    environment: pypi
    permissions:
      id-token: write

    steps:
      - name: Download artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: mariadb-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: dist/

      - name: Publish mariadb to PyPI
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
        with:
          packages-dir: dist/
          skip-existing: true
          verbose: true
",
  "rationale": "Added pip dependency caching to the build-sdist job using actions/cache@v4, keyed by runner OS and pyproject.toml hash. This follows the measured pattern from evidence (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2) where caching ~/.cache/pip reduced repeated dependency fetch time. The build-sdist job installs build dependencies (build, setuptools, wheel, packaging) on every run; caching these downloads preserves all build/test coverage while saving CI resources on repeated workflow dispatches. The Windows wheel job already caches MariaDB Connector/C and uses cibuildwheel which manages its own Python environment; no change needed there. No permissions weakened, no new secrets or network access added.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]
}

Let me analyze this workflow and the evidence to determine if there's a suitable CI optimization.

The workflow is a release workflow that:
1. Builds sdist on Ubuntu
2. Builds Windows wheels for multiple Python versions and architectures
3. Merges wheels
4. Publishes to TestPyPI or PyPI

Looking at the evidence, I see several patterns. The most relevant ones for this workflow appear to be:

1. **P-LIT-GHA-CACHE** - Cache dependency downloads (has measured benefit)
2. **P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE** - Share cached build dependencies (secondary report only)
3. **P-LIT-ENV-CACHE** - Reuse validated build environments (reported benefit)
4. **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** - Bound jobs with custom timeout (estimated benefit)

Let me check the workflow for caching opportunities:

1. The `build-sdist` job installs MariaDB Connector/C development files and Python build dependencies
2. The `build-wheels-windows` job uses cibuildwheel and caches MariaDB Connector/C build
3. There's already a cache step for MariaDB Connector/C on Windows

Looking at the evidence, the first evidence item (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2) shows adding a pip cache to a Python workflow. This is pattern P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE.

The workflow already has:
- A cache for MariaDB Connector/C on Windows (`actions/cache@v6` with path `C:\\mariadb-connector-c.build`)
- But no pip cache for Python dependencies

The `build-sdist` job installs:
- `libmariadb-dev` via apt
- Python packages: `build`, `setuptools`, `wheel`, `packaging`

The `build-wheels-windows` job uses cibuildwheel which will install Python dependencies.

Since this is a release workflow that runs on `release` published and `workflow_dispatch`, it doesn't run frequently. However, when it does run, it builds multiple matrix combinations on Windows.

Let me check if there's a pip cache that could be added. The evidence shows adding:
```yaml
- name: Cache pip dependencies
  uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
    path: ~/.cache/pip
    key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
    restore-keys: |
      ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
```

This would cache pip dependencies. The workflow uses `pyproject.toml` (we can see from repository_context), so the hashFiles would work.

However, I need to check if this workflow already has pip caching. Looking at the workflow:
- `build-sdist` job: No pip cache
- `build-wheels-windows` job: No pip cache (only MariaDB Connector/C cache)
- `merge-wheels`, `publish-testpypi`, `publish-pypi`: No pip install steps

The `build-sdist` job runs `pip install build setuptools wheel packaging` - these could be cached.
The `build-wheels-windows` job uses cibuildwheel which internally installs dependencies.

The evidence from the first experiment shows adding pip cache to a Python workflow with pattern P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE. The similarity is 0.65.

But wait - the pattern catalogue shows P-LIT-GHA-CACHE as "Cache dependency downloads" with reported benefit (vm_time_reduction_percent: free 6%, paid 3.4%). This seems more directly applicable.

P-LIT-GHA-CACHE preconditions:
- Repeated dependency fetching is measurable
- Cache inputs include lockfile and environment

The workflow doesn't have a lockfile (requirements.txt or poetry.lock), but it has pyproject.toml. The evidence example uses hashFiles('pyproject.toml').

However, this is a release workflow that runs infrequently (only on release published or manual dispatch). The benefit of caching might be minimal since it doesn't run on every push.

Let me also consider P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT - the workflow has matrix builds on Windows that could potentially hang. But there's no timeout set.

Looking at the jobs:
- `build-sdist`: Single job, could benefit from timeout
- `build-wheels-windows`: Matrix of 2 arches × 5 Python versions = 10 jobs, could benefit from timeout
- `merge-wheels`: Simple merge
- `publish-testpypi`/`publish-pypi`: Publish steps

The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern has estimated benefit (vm_time_reduction_percent: free 12.9%, paid 8.1%).

But the instruction says "Preserve the intended build and test coverage, and avoid unrelated changes." Adding timeouts could be considered a safety improvement rather than an optimization.

Let me re-read the evidence more carefully. The first evidence item shows a measured CI workflow on a fork where they added pip caching. The pattern is P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE.

The pattern catalogue shows P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE as "Share cached build dependencies" with secondary_report_only status.

For `build-sdist`, it's a straightforward pip install that could benefit from caching.

```yaml
- name: Install build dependencies
  run: |
    python -m pip install --upgrade pip
    pip install build setuptools wheel packaging
```

These are build dependencies, not runtime dependencies. They're fixed versions (no version constraints shown), so caching could help.

But since this workflow runs only on release/workflow_dispatch, the cache hit rate might be low unless the same version is built multiple times.

```yaml
          python-version: "3.13"

        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install '.[dev]'
```

So I should add a similar step to the build-sdist job after "Set up Python" and before "Install build dependencies".

For the build-wheels-windows job, it uses cibuildwheel which handles its own Python environment. Adding a pip cache there might not be straightforward or necessary.

Let me create the updated workflow with the pip cache added to build-sdist job.

Also, I should consider if the merge-wheels, publish-testpypi, publish-pypi jobs need any optimization. They download artifacts and publish - not much to optimize there.

The evidence_ids should include the first evidence item (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2) and possibly the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern from the catalogue.

Wait, the instruction says "Use only supported evidence IDs; APPLY requires at least one." The evidence IDs are the document_ids from the evidence array. The first evidence has document_id: "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2". The pattern catalogue items have document_id like "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE".

I should use the evidence IDs from the evidence array provided, not the pattern catalogue. The evidence array has 6 items, all with document_id starting with "experiment:" or "pattern:".

Actually, looking at the evidence array, the first item has document_id: "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2" and pattern_id: "P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE".

The pattern catalogue is separate context. The instruction says "Use retrieved evidence and repository files to check prerequisites." and "Use only supported evidence IDs".

The evidence IDs are the document_id fields from the evidence array. So I should use "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2" as evidence_id.

But the pattern catalogue also has document_ids like "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE". Are those considered evidence IDs? The instruction says "retrieved evidence" which includes both the evidence array and the pattern catalogue.

Let me re-read: "Use retrieved evidence and repository files to check prerequisites." and "Use only supported evidence IDs; APPLY requires at least one."

The evidence array is provided in the input under "evidence". The pattern_catalogue is also provided. Both are retrieved evidence.

I think I can use either. The first evidence item directly shows adding pip cache to a Python workflow, which is very similar to what we need.

Let me proceed with APPLY, adding pip cache to the build-sdist job, using the first evidence item as support.

I'll also add a timeout to the build-sdist job and build-wheels-windows job using P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern, but that might be considered unrelated. The instruction says "avoid unrelated changes". Adding cache is directly related to the evidence. Adding timeout is a different pattern.

I'll stick with just the pip cache addition for now.
